applicability: code-level messages naming an authority; excludes prompts, which are writer behavior by construction
destination: AGENTS.md Adding a defensive branch to a fleet script (diagnostic-message twin)

evidence.source_reference: PR #116 3ee9c38 workflows/deep-review.js guard and scope dispatch

expected_behavior: A diagnostic states what was actually compared. Where it names an external authority as the source of truth, the comparison is against a value independently obtained from that authority -- captured once and reused is fine -- never against a copy the compared party authored itself.
observation: A workflow guard compared two fields of one agent-reported packet -- candidate_sha and its own declared alias head_sha, both produced by a single delegated 'git rev-parse HEAD' the scope agent was asked to run -- and reported their disagreement as 'scope candidate_sha did not match git HEAD'. Git was consulted, but not by the comparison: the guard cannot tell which copy is wrong, and names an authority it did not re-read, sending an operator to check a value that matches.
reason: Landed 2026-08-20: defensive-branch playbook now requires a diagnostic naming an external authority to compare against a value independently obtained from it.
